title: The self-service acceptance has no named operation, no access right and no declared owner of its cross-service rows, and the legacy key carries a screen and a permission check of the module template
source: Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3, RWB-E4-036 Accept an offer in self-service sections 1 to 16; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.15 and A1.2; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1 and T6.1; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-RES-16, R-SET-10, R-DIL-18, R-RES-19, R-SET-12, R-UNI-04, R-UNI-10); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 5 Exception paths; 7 Acceptance criteria; 10 Authority; 12.1 to 12.4; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states
description: The legacy story and the FSD A2.15 describe the capability as a customer action on LINE OA and HOME.SCB that records the acceptance on the case, and no source names the operation that takes it, its request, its answer, its errors or its access right: the TSD P6 endpoint inventory stops at API-P6-011 and holds no acceptance path, TSD P6 T6.1 lists staff roles only and names no customer role, and the legacy permission check names Litigation C and R, which is the module template's copy. The three cross-service facts the capability needs are named in no plan row: the case stage on rwb-case, the contact point and its consent on rwb-source-data (DP-05) and the contact stop on rwb-deviation. The plan declares no C row for any of them. The catalogue holds no acceptance event, the second acceptance of the same notice has no rule and no message, the tap outside the offer-with-customer stages has no message ID, and screen SCR-33 Template approval, which the legacy story names, is the template screen of the same module and not a customer-facing acceptance. This row gathers every missing value of the app story and the story cites it wherever the placeholder stands.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 lists API-P6-001 to API-P6-011 only, none of them an acceptance; TSD P6 T6.1 rows are staff and partner roles only; legacy RWB-E4-036 permission table rows read Litigation C and Litigation R; the WP dependency lists of RWB-P6-E4036-APP carry no C row; Architecture v5 slide 42 names NoticeGenerated, NoticeDispatched and NoticeDelivered on rwb.comms.events.v1 and no acceptance event; FSD P6 A2.15 section A2.15.4 carries the generic criteria of the auto-generated entry
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-comms, with the rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-deviation and gateway-bff owners and the access owner of rwb-access
proposed: Fix the two operations as POST and GET /cases/{caseId}/offer-acceptances on /api/recovery/comms/v1 with capability area Case record (right C for the POST, right R for the GET), declare the three consumed rows as consumed and faked until their C rows exist, declare no acceptance event, and fix the two unnamed refusal texts in the RWB-P6-E4036-CON review

title: No requirement row covers FEAT-COM-02, so the acceptance has no requirement ID to trace to
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T8 Requirement traceability; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A1.2
description: The P6 requirement table of TSD P6 T8 stops at REQ-OCC-011, which maps to FEAT-COM-01, and holds no row for FEAT-COM-02. The FSD P6 A1.2 lists FEAT-COM-02 as one of the eight Epic 4 features of the module, and no requirement ID, BRD section or L3 process is attached to it in any source read for this key. The app story and the contract story therefore trace to the feature and the rules and not to a requirement.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T8 rows REQ-OCC-001 to REQ-OCC-011, the last mapped to FEAT-COM-01 with the story Written one epic ahead; FSD P6 v3 A1.2 row FEAT-COM-02 with First in E4 and section A2.15
owner_role: Business analyst of P6, with the requirement owner of the Epic 4 BRD
proposed: The Epic 4 BRD gives FEAT-COM-02 a requirement ID in the P6 list at the next revision; until then both stories trace to the feature, the rules VR-P6-015-1, VR-P6-015-2 and BR-P6-015 and the routing rows R-RES-16, R-SET-10 and R-DIL-18

title: The contract baseline of the acceptance fixes two operations, one access right, one decision mapping and five error conditions for which no source gives a name, a type or a message
source: _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Technical Specifications by Module v5/Recovery Workbench TSD P6 Communications v2 T-A.1, T-A.2, T6.1 and T8; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Functional Specifications by Module v6/Recovery Workbench FSD P6 Communications v3 A2.15; Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3, RWB-E4-036; _work/msr/extract/Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4; Template and Rules v1 R5.5 and R9
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12.1 to 12.8; 13 Solution plan; 14 Validation and messages; 15 Screens and states
description: The contract baseline has to fix what no source fixes: the two acceptance paths, the elements and types of the request and the answer, the access right of a customer-facing tap, the three consumed rows whose owners publish no operation for this key, the decision code and the rule of an acceptance as a mapping of three stage codes, the message of the offer-not-with-customer condition and of a second acceptance, and the statement that no acceptance event, table, workflow or Schedule exists. TSD P6 T-A.1 holds no acceptance operation, T6.1 names no customer role, T8 holds no requirement, and the routing table names the states, the rules and the decision sets D5, D6 and D6.4 without naming the message of either refusal. This row gathers every missing value of the contract story and the story cites it wherever the placeholder stands.
evidence: TSD P6 v2 T-A.1 and T-A.2 stop at API-P6-011; TSD P6 T6.1 has no customer role; Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 rows R-RES-16, R-SET-10, R-DIL-18 and R-DIL-19 give the decision sets D5, D6 and D6.4 and no message ID; Architecture v5 slide 42 lists three events for rwb-comms and none for an acceptance
owner_role: Tech lead of rwb-comms and solution architect, with the rwb-case, rwb-source-data, rwb-deviation, rwb-decision and gateway-bff owners
proposed: Publish the two operations and their closed sets in the rwb-comms OpenAPI document, declare the three consumed rows as consumed and faked, carry the stage-to-decision-code-and-rule mapping as a versioned configuration row, and fix the two unnamed refusal texts in the baseline review before the first consumer signs off
